A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C-BOD research. All 10 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and v2 Appendices A–C, support comparison. V1 has no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original MMLU experiments on 26 LLMs, including accuracy changes, significance outcomes, scaling analyses, and examples.

after.justification: V2 reports original MMLU and GPQA experiments, including proprietary GPT models, multiple rephrasing conditions, and semantic-fidelity assessments.

M1.justification: The perturb-and-compare detector and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. V2 refines perturbation generation through a substantially more constrained rephrasing prompt and semantic verification with iterative correction before evaluation (Section 4.1.1 and Appendix A), extending v1's formatting checks and manual audits.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only MMLU. V2 adds GPQA's 546 graduate-level reasoning questions, with actual results in Appendix C and Table 5. This extends evaluated task coverage beyond the original general-knowledge benchmark.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing overfitting-detection methods against C-BOD. Changes to the tested LLM roster and rephrasing models concern evaluation targets and configurations.

E3.justification: V1 uses DeepSeek rephrasing at temperature 1.0 on MMLU. V2 adds Claude 3.5 Haiku at 0.5, GPQA evaluations at 0.5/1.0/1.5, and a substantially revised panel of 27 open-weight and five proprietary models. Reported MMLU manual-audit coverage increases from approximately 10% to 20%; GPQA coverage is 50%.

E4.justification: V2 adds semantic-fidelity analyses using Sentence-BERT and an o3 judge, a GPQA temperature sweep, and proprietary-model generation/robustness analyses. The case-study table expands from four examples to six; the four retained examples are reattributed from Qwen2.5-32B to Qwen3-14B.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same paired McNemar chi-squared test with one degree of freedom and a 0.05 significance threshold. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Additional significance outcomes use the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for Claude rephrasings, five GPT models, three GPQA temperatures, and semantic similarity. Retained entries also change: Llama-1B's original accuracy rises from a reported 26.98% in v1 Table 2 to 28.11% in v2 Table 1, while perturbed accuracy 27.00% and the reported -0.08% change remain. Changed conditions and internal inconsistencies prevent interpreting these revisions as matched-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the transformation definition, paired comparison function, discordant counts, McNemar statistic, and decision rule. Equation edits clarify notation and parentheses; no substantive theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central detection claim and interpretation of benchmark sensitivity remain. V2 removes v1's standalone Blueprint for Iterative Overfit Mitigation contribution and replaces the abstract's training-pipeline integration claim with evaluation-pipeline integration and a prospective foundation for mitigation.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 introduces interpretations that newer and larger proprietary GPT variants generalize better, adding a different scaling interpretation from the retained overall sensitivity claim. Appendix C attributes less consistent GPQA effects to benchmark novelty, low accuracy, limited statistical power, and reasoning difficulty. The existing Section 8 limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A provides detailed system/user rephrasing instructions, the semantic-judge prompt, and prompt-refinement procedures. V2 also documents similarity thresholds, audit criteria, dataset sizes, and additional generator settings, and changes the repository pointer. Reproducibility remains imperfect: Section 4.1 identifies the GPQA generator as GPT-4o-mini, whereas Appendix C names GPT-4o.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for GPQA, Zephyr, and the GPT comparison discussion, while removing specific contamination-detection and model-editing discussions and citations, including Lee, Li, and Zhang. The core positioning—benchmark-structure overfitting as distinct from training-data contamination—remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and contributions are revised, related work is reorganized into three subsections, and new appendices organize supporting material. The affiliation line also changes. The principal section sequence and substantial portions of the method, discussion, conclusion, and limitations remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, and the main MMLU table is restructured into two rephrasing-condition blocks. Scaling and accuracy plots are reorganized by condition, replacing the earlier split-by-size display. V2 adds GPT and GPQA tables and a GPT plot, expands the case-study display, and relocates the model inventory to Appendix B.

improvement.justification: Broader experiments and detailed semantic-validation procedures strengthen coverage and reproducibility. However, v2 introduces material reporting contradictions: Table 1 labels Gemma-12B's 68.71% to 68.77% accuracy change as a 3.20% decline, and the abstract presents 2.75% as the average drop although Section 5.1 assigns it to the significant-results subset. These problems weaken the expanded empirical case. The PDFs do not establish whether they are isolated reporting errors or affect the conclusions, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
